review.statement: For all sufficiently large perfect-square n, put n qubits on a square grid and apply n³ layers cycling through the four horizontal and vertical even and odd nearest-neighbor matchings. Draw each two-qubit gate independently from Haar measure and specify it to operator-norm precision 2⁻ⁿ³ with polynomially many bits. Let p_C be the ideal computational-basis output law from |0ⁿ⟩. For any uniform randomized polynomial-time classical sampler S with output law q_C, does Pr_C[dTV(q_C,p_C) ≤ 1/n] ≥ 1−1/n for all sufficiently large n imply that the polynomial hierarchy collapses, using only standard worst-case complexity assumptions? The outer probability is over circuits. The sampler's random bits define q_C. [Catalogue A13](https://openquantumproblems.com/p/A13)
review.significance: The claim would turn an ideal random-circuit experiment into a complexity-theoretic separation under the usual noncollapse assumption for the polynomial hierarchy. It requires hardness for the full output law of a typical circuit, with an explicit error budget and circuit success fraction.
review.settlement_test: A proof must derive a polynomial-hierarchy collapse from a sampler meeting the stated depth, layout, encoding, total-variation error and circuit success guarantees, without assuming average-case random-circuit hardness. A direct reduction would work, as would a worst-case hardness reduction to probability estimation at an error and success rate that the sampler can supply. A polynomial-time sampler meeting the same guarantees would refute the hardness prediction under polynomial-hierarchy noncollapse.
review.aliases: Approximate random-circuit sampling (approximate RCS) and total-variation hardness of ideal RCS. The cross-listed title 'Average-case approximation hardness of random-circuit output probabilities' refers to BFNV Conjecture 6, which asks for hardness of estimating a single output probability on some fixed layout family. A13 fixes a particular layout and asks about sampling. [QIQCOP cross-list](https://qiqc-op.com/problem/op_94fc1874fe23df16/) [BFNV preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04402)
review.attempt:
I checked A13 against the cross-listed conjecture and compared the cited results by task, error scale and assumptions. BFNV and Movassagh establish exact-probability hardness, and Krovi gives high-precision hardness at a 2⁻ᴼ⁽ᵐ⁾ tolerance for m gates. Bouland et al. v2, Appendix B, reaches 2⁻ⁿ⁻ᴼ⁽ⁿᵞ⁾ for arbitrarily small fixed γ>0 in its covered ensembles. Go–Oh–Jeong v1 assumes ideal average-case hardness to derive noisy sampling hardness. Sen–Hunter-Jones v1 studies the distribution of a fixed output probability over random circuits. I found no settlement of A13 in these sources. [BFNV](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04402) [Movassagh v4](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.06210) [Krovi](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.05642) [Bouland et al. v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.04566) [Go–Oh–Jeong v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20804) [Sen–Hunter-Jones v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02125)

I checked the sampler-to-estimator error budget. On each good circuit, a uniform output label X gives E_X|p_C(X)−q_C(X)| ≤ 2/(n·2ⁿ) and E_X q_C(X)=2⁻ⁿ. By Markov's inequality, the respective bounds 16/(n·2ⁿ) and 8·2⁻ⁿ each fail on at most 1/8 of labels. Stockmeyer approximate counting at relative error 1/n, with failure at most 1/16, then estimates p_C(X) to additive error 24/(n·2ⁿ), with joint failure at most 5/16+1/n over circuits, labels and counting randomness. This calculation retains X as part of the estimator input.
review.remaining_obligation: Prove or disprove this sufficient lemma: on the exact finite-precision A13 ensemble, an oracle that estimates p_C(X) to additive error 24/(n·2ⁿ) with joint success at least 2/3 for a random circuit and independent uniform label X lets a randomized polynomial-time reduction with NP access solve a worst-case #P-complete counting problem. The reduction must tolerate arbitrary errors on the remaining inputs, including failures correlated with the circuit. The calculation in attempt supplies the oracle guarantee asymptotically if the sampler exists. The worst-case reduction remains open in this intake.
review.human_brief: Initialize a grid of qubits in zero, apply random two-qubit gates to disjoint neighboring pairs in each layer, then measure every qubit to get a bit string. Repeating the same circuit builds its output distribution. For a two-qubit toy circuit, a gate sending |00⟩ to (|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2 gives 00 and 11 with probability 1/2 each. Uniform guessing assigns 1/4 to each of four strings, so its total-variation error is 1/2. If hardware errors accumulate over the n³ layers, test the reduction first with noiseless circuit descriptions. Hardware samples would instead test a noise-dependent claim.
